<question>
what is company goodwill and why important
</question>

<reference>

passage 3:When a business has provided good service or product to their customers, the customers develop a trust for the business. They become repeat customers and they tell others what … a good experience they had. That creates a business asset called goodwill, in other words the good will of the customers toward the business. Answer 2 The goodwill of a business is the whole advantage of the reputation and connection with customers together with the circumstances whether of habit or otherwise, which tend to make that connection permanent. It represents in connection with any business or business product the value of the attraction to the customers which the name and reputation possesses.
</reference>

<answer>
Goodwill in a business refers to the advantage gained from the reputation and connection with customers. It represents the value of the attraction the business holds for customers based on its name and reputation. Goodwill is important because it helps increase the customer base, retain old clients, attract investors, and attract potential buyers. It is built when a business consistently provides good service or products, creating trust and positive experiences among customers.
</answer>

How to decide:
- A claim is supported when the reference answer or a current source article states it, or it follows directly from them. Rewording, writing "$5.00" as "$5", and leaving details out are fine.
- A claim is unsupported when it adds a number, fee, limit, time, plan detail, product, step or rule that the reference and the current sources do not state, or states one differently. One unsupported claim is enough to fail "grounded".
- Check every number against the plan it is about. A value that belongs to another plan is wrong.
- An article marked as superseded shows an old version of a policy. It does not support a claim, unless the question asks what changed.
- Courtesy text such as "message us in the app if you need more help" is not a factual claim.
